statement.text: Let $\pi(n; a, b)$ be the number of primes $p \le n$ with $p \equiv a \pmod b$. For every $a$ and $b$ with $a \perp b$, are there infinitely many values of $n$ for which $\pi(n; a, b) > \pi(n; a_1, b)$ for every $a_1 \not\equiv a \pmod b$?

title: The Prime Number Race
